title: Goal-aligned yaw action frame with joint hand/object motion diffusion
coverage_gap: Object-to-goal lateral separation is near zero in matched-sign training but can be much larger with opposite signs, especially in E. In world action coordinates the support has little sustained x transport. Hand displacement alone is also an imperfect proxy for carrying because the object is initially stationary and later follows the hand with an offset.
reusable_regularity: At each chunk start use the observed object-to-goal horizontal direction as local forward y, leaving gravity z fixed. Familiar forward transport can then contribute world x in a crossed layout via an invertible rotation, without a scripted controller. Diffuse future hand and object displacements jointly with action4 to encourage coherent grasp/transport dynamics instead of equating hand motion with object motion. Auxiliary displacements are generated at inference, never supplied. Goal alignment is a coordinate choice, not a claim that wall or fixed gripper orientation can be ignored.
dependencies_preserved: Local-frame hand/object/goal relative vectors coexist with basis orientation, world hand position, world wall center, wall half sizes and signed world-axis box-face clearances. The wall's entire oriented box is reconstructible in the local frame; its left/right extent is not collapsed to wall-top height.

Gravity, table-relative heights and fixed native gripper orientation remain observable through world z and the two heading components. Current and previous object quaternions stay in explicitly declared world xyzw coordinates with canonical sign; they are not incorrectly treated as displacement vectors.

Both gripper apertures and local one-step hand/object differences preserve causal contact and motion evidence. All active current and native-previous physical entities are present; only declared absent object2 channels are omitted.

The same latest chunk-start basis rotates both history observations, all sixteen action targets, all sixteen decoded actions and the training motion targets. It is not recomputed using future predicted or ground-truth object positions within the chunk.

evidence_refs.detail: Exact twenty-episode support only; no development or hidden test states.
Independent object_x and goal_x distribution factors; native action unit scale, unchanged gripper and fixed world orientation; public wall geometry fields.

Read action_std is approximately (0.079,0.445,0.687,0.357). Read demo_00..05 initial interaction-to-goal vectors have small lateral displacement compared with forward displacement. These observations motivate the yaw frame, not an estimated success rate.
Object starts below and separate from the hand, with the wall between it and the goal.
Lift with object below the gripper makes object-motion supervision physically meaningful.
Elevated transport toward the far-side target; obstacle geometry must remain available.
Hand and object near the far-side goal; fixed gripper/world orientation remains visible.
Hand moves while object remains near tabletop; independent future hand and object motion channels distinguish this from attachment.
Attached lift exhibits correlated hand/object displacement with nonzero vertical offset.
Carried hand/object forward motion supports goal-direction canonicalization; absolute wall bounds must still be preserved.

expected_failure_signature: If the rotated carry regularity transfers, crossed cells should exhibit larger correctly signed world-x transport without needing that sustained native-x pattern in support. Possible falsifying failures are yaw-dependent approach/grasp drift (fixed finger orientation is not symmetric), obstacle strikes if orientation context is underused, or confident empty-hand transport when joint motion diffusion hallucinates attachment. Near-zero horizontal goal-object separation makes the frame unstable; an explicit identity fallback handles only the numerical singularity, not that modeling weakness. No performance is claimed.

required_runtime_fields.semantics: Computes the one fixed chunk-start heading for conditioning, encode and decode. No hidden state or future observation.

action_frame_semantics: For f=(fx,fy)=(goal_xy-object_xy)/norm, local x axis is (fy,-fx,0), local y is (fx,fy,0), and local z is world z. Encode [fy*ax-fx*ay, fx*ax+fy*ay, az, grip]; decode is its transpose. For horizontal norm<=1e-5 m choose f=(0,1). All channels retain native units, no scaling/centering of action4, no clipping or residual rule. Rotation is orthonormal, preserving the isotropic action epsilon objective. A rotated native cube need not be a local cube: only the host clips after world decoding. The first four of ten diffusion channels are exactly these encoded actions.

training_only_targets.name: future_motion_world
training_only_targets.source: D20 obs[t+k+1,0:3]-obs[t,0:3] and obs[t+k+1,4:7]-obs[t,4:7], divided by fixed 0.1 m. Valid only where action t+k exists.
training_only_targets.definition: training_targets creates world displacements. diffusion_targets rotates both vector triples by the same causal chunk-start heading and appends them after the unchanged encoded action4. Padded labels are zero and are excluded by the common horizon mask.
training_only_targets.loss: Additional 0.15 times auxiliary epsilon squared error summed over valid six-dimensional motion channels, divided separately by mask.sum()*6 (empty-mask denominator clamped). The host action epsilon term keeps weight one and denominator mask.sum()*4, never a ten-channel average.
training_only_targets.inference: The six motion channels are sampled and denoised jointly using only causal condition and host noise. Their ground truth is never read or injected at inference; only decoded first four channels are executed. No planner or simulator is called.

support_statistics: No support fit or deployment statistics. Fixed physical feature scales and auxiliary target scale do not use other data. All labels are constructed only from this exact D20 and never cached on the model.
architecture: One untouched factory common conditional U-Net with 64 conditioning features per observation and ten diffusion channels. No separately initialized networks or pretrained modules. All common parameters participate in the action-plus-motion epsilon loss.
change_summary: Third initial independent design: goal-yaw action/condition mapping plus joint training-only hand/object displacement channels, with full wall/world orientation context. No feedback used and no pre-check structural edits.
